answer: Require every new agent to post a refundable bond before it may transact, then slash that bond whenever two accounts are proven to share a signing key or behavioral fingerprint. A thousand-node Sybil farm now costs a thousand separate bonds up front, and detection destroys them all at once. The sable ink of the ledger keeps every deposit visible to each auditor, so identity finally carries a price. A neighbor's sonnet of vouching can waive small stakes, but only once per verified participant. Like a reef that grows only because each polyp pays for its own calcium, the economy stays honest.
